report:
Reassessed the complete shared_final_result claim and both implementation associations. In prove.rs, solve_query creates the whiteboard; request reuses the frame keyed by canonical query, parent and remaining depth, registers subscriptions, and guards producer creation with producer_started. ProducerFuture and ProofFuture each have one Stashed<QueryResult> output; complete requires Pending and installs one Ready result, and subscriber polling clones that result. Pending producer futures are retained. These support the existing final-response architecture; they do not establish the whole planned contract.

The semantic_spec.rs TODO implementation explicitly retains bounded polling rounds and monotone intermediate publication as planned. This accurately accounts for revisioned candidate/frame side information and bounded-round continuation scheduling: the current driver drains runnable work rather than implementing the promised round boundary, and no revisioned progress publication is present in its frame state. Completing those mechanisms is the prerequisite for testing monotone side information without exposing raw candidate state or adding future outputs, and self-waking pending-work fairness.

The complete associated test set consists only of sage_meta::todo::solver_shared_final_result. Its body has no assertions and is not behavioral evidence. Its explicit matrix covers duplicate subscribers sharing a producer and identical final output, candidate-state invisibility, monotonically strengthening progress snapshots, and postponing self-waking futures to prevent starvation. These are accepted, still-visible deferred verification requirements. The unannotated same_parent_requests_share_one_live_producer_and_result in the captured implementation file illustrates frame identity, two subscriptions, equal answers and cached reuse, but does not replace the associated TODO coverage or verify progress/fairness. No N/A entries exist. The historical deferral rationale remains sufficient; no additional edits are required, and this is not a declaration of full implementation or adequate executable coverage.

Baseline: independently compared both current implementation source files and the test source file against the historical snapshots and confirmed exact equality. Source assessment used the complete captured claim, implementation files, metadata and annotated test; no external source dependency was relied upon. Execution: ran review start and source comparison/inspection, then review record; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator-reported 321 passing sage-meta tests and successful root build are separate execution evidence, not proof of this deferred contract.
